docs.text: JomForm Docs — Overview & features Every JomForm feature in one line, grouped by category: start here, sales & payments, forms & fields, storefront, email, growth, security and developer guides. Workspaces (your account's tenant) A workspace holds your forms, products, sales and payment account, and owns its own address ({slug}.jomform.com or your domain). With none, the dashboard asks you to create one. Renaming a workspace Rename a workspace's name or its public address; the old address keeps redirecting. Deleting a workspace Reversible, not destructive: a typed slug confirmation sends it to the Trash, even a full workspace. Restoring is one click; deleting for good is a second step that refuses one with sales. Activity log (audit trail) Every action in this workspace, newest first, including the destructive ones — a deletion leaves no other trace. Append-only. Sales Track every sale: reference code, status, buyer, amount, payment method and date. Confirm bank transfers, capture or release authorisations, refund, and export CSV. One list for sales and responses Without a form filter the Sales page is one merged list: every sale and every response, newest first, with one combined count. Responses (response-only forms) A form can collect answers instead of payments. Its entries are stored as responses, shown on the same Sales page, with a drawer holding every value. Form analytics (the per-form counter) The per-form counter counts the rows that form actually recorded: responses for a response form, sales in every status for a payment form. Never both. Partial refunds Refund a paid sale in full or in part: the sale records how much was returned and keeps the balance refundable until zero.

docs.title: The form builder
docs.description: How the JomForm form builder works: the field palette, the canvas, editing a block's settings on desktop and on a phone, and the per-block actions.
docs.text: JomForm Docs — the form builder How the JomForm form builder works: the field palette, the canvas, editing a block's settings on desktop and on a phone, and the per-block actions. The three areas The builder is where a form's fields are laid out. It is the same surface for a form and for one of your own templates. On a desktop (768px and wider) the builder is three columns. The field palette on the left holds every field type, grouped Standard, Advanced and Pricing. The canvas in the middle holds the fields in the order a buyer sees them. The block settings panel on the right edits whichever block is selected. Adding a field Drag a palette item onto the canvas, or tap it. A tap appends the field to the end. On a phone the palette lives behind the Add tab. Adding a field returns you to the canvas with the new block highlighted, so you can add several in a row without leaving the canvas. Editing a block's settings Every block has settings: its label or text, description, placeholder, CSS class, inline style, required flag and validation message. A field type that needs one also gets a choices editor, a product picker or a conditional-logic rule. Which settings appear depends on the type. On a desktop, tap a block on the canvas and its settings appear in the right-hand panel. On a phone, tap a block and the settings panel replaces the canvas. The row at the top of the panel is ← Canvas next to the block's type. It returns you to the canvas. The block stays highlighted after you close the panel, and tapping it again reopens its settings. The mobile tab bar has two tabs, Add and Canvas. There is no separate settings tab: editing a block is a tap on the block itself. What each setting does Every one of these reaches the published form.

docs.title: Affiliate programme: setup guide
docs.description: Give someone a link, and the sales that arrive through it are attributed to them with a commission on every paid sale. Every screenshot here was captured from the running product; the red box marks…
docs.text: Give someone a link, and the sales that arrive through it are attributed to them with a commission on every paid sale. Every screenshot here was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: an affiliate is a code in a workspace. A sale that arrives with that code attached is attributed to the affiliate. The commission you set here is computed on the paid sale, not on the form view and not on an abandoned checkout. 1. Create the affiliate Settings → Affiliates . Fill Code (the short code that goes in the link, SITI here), Name (who it belongs to), Commission % (10 here) and press Add affiliate . The code is unique inside the workspace; a second SITI is refused with code already exists . 2. Hand over the link The new row carries the affiliate's own link: https://<workspace .jomform.com/?aff=SITI . Anything a visitor buys after opening that URL is attributed to SITI, and 10% of the paid amount is her commission. The code is per workspace, so the same person promoting two workspaces has two links. How the commission is counted - Only paid sales count. A commission exists because a payment settled. An unpaid checkout, a refused card or a form response with no product contributes nothing. - The sale records the code, not the money. Each sale carries the affiliate code that brought it in, and the commission is the affiliate's rate applied to that sale. The row above is the one place the percentage lives. - Cancelling a card never revokes anything on the affiliate side. Attribution follows the sale record, not the card token. Notes - One code per promotion, not per person. A merchant tracking two channels (a WhatsApp group and an Instagram bio) uses two codes, and each channel gets its own commission line.

docs.text: One membership, one fee that repeats, and nobody has to remember to pay next year. Every screenshot here was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: a membership is a single Subscription product, monthly or yearly, sold from any payment form. The member pays once with a card at checkout; the card is saved, and the same card is charged every period after that. There is no spreadsheet of who has paid and no bank transfer to reconcile. 1. Create the plan as a Subscription product Products → Product name (here Keahlian Kelab 2026 ), Price (RM) 240.00, then change Type to Subscription and set Billing period to Yearly (or Monthly for a monthly club). Billing count Infinite (recurring) means it renews until cancelled. Next charge date From the day it succeeds starts the cycle on the first successful payment. 2. Check the plan in the catalogue The row reads Subscription · Yearly · RM240.00 . That one row is the whole plan. Every member of the club is sold this same product, so a price change is a single edit here. 3. Sell it from a payment form Forms → New form → Blank form , then add Product under PRICING FIELDS , Name and Email . Select the Product block and pick the plan in BLOCK SETTINGS → Product . A Section block under the email is worth the thirty seconds it costs: it renders as prose, where a Note block would render an input the member has to fill. That is where you tell the member the fee renews. 4. Publish and hand out the link Publish makes the form live and the banner gives you the address ( …/f/keahlian-kelab-2026 ). Copy link is what goes to the members: one link for the whole club, no per-member form. 5.

docs.title: Design with an AI agent (MCP): setup guide
docs.description: JomForm speaks the Model Context Protocol. Connect your AI agent once and it can drive the store with plain language: add products, edit forms, read sales, refund a sale. Every screenshot here was…
headings: 1. Open the connect page and copy the server URL
2. Paste it into your MCP client
docs.text: JomForm speaks the Model Context Protocol. Connect your AI agent once and it can drive the store with plain language: add products, edit forms, read sales, refund a sale. Every screenshot here was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. 1. Open the connect page and copy the server URL The MCP page ( /mcp on your JomForm address) is the whole setup, and it prints the one thing you need: https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp . The /mcp path is required: mcp.jomform.com without it fails. Press Copy . 2. Paste it into your MCP client Claude Desktop reads its servers from claude desktop config.json ; the page prints the exact entry ( {"mcpServers": {"jomform": {"type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp"}}} ). Any other client that supports a remote MCP server over HTTP takes the same URL instead. Restart the client after saving. 3. Authorise The client fetches the server, finds the OAuth 2.1 (PKCE) endpoints itself and opens a JomForm login or authorise page. Sign in and grant access. There is no API key to copy and no token to rotate : the grant is the credential. 4. Pick the scope The client asks for a scope and the grant is enforced on every tool call: scope what the agent can do --- --- read look at forms, products, sales and analytics. Every tool that creates, updates, deletes, archives, cancels or refunds is refused with a scope error readwrite do all of that and change the store: add a product, edit a form, refund a sale A client that asks for no scope gets readwrite . A read-only grant cannot upgrade itself: it is refused on the tool that mints API keys, so it can never manufacture a wider credential. 5. Ask for what you want That is the whole interface from here on.

docs.text: A step-by-step guide to taking donations with a JomForm payment form. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the one control you touch at that step. What this does: a donation is a normal payment form, and an amount is a product . There are two shapes of donation product: - Fixed denominations : one product per amount you accept ( Donation RM10 , Donation RM50 , Donation RM100 ), and the donor ticks the one they want. Steps 2–8 below walk this shape. - Pay what you want : a single product set to Pay what you want (donation) . The form shows the donor an amount field instead of a price, and the amount is checked against the limits you set. See the first two Notes. Either way the money lands in the same sale list and receipt flow as any other paid form. 1. Connect CHIP Collect in Settings Settings → CHIP . Paste the Brand ID and Secret Key from the CHIP Merchant Portal, pick the Mode the key was created in there (Test or Live), and save. The mode is a label you choose, because the key itself carries no hint of which one it is. That save is what turns the form's pay button into a working payment. 2. Add your first donation amount in Products Products → type the name ( Donation RM10 ), the price ( 10.00 ), leave Type on One-time , then Add product . The price you type is exactly what the donor pays for that tier. 3. Add the other amounts Repeat step 2 for Donation RM50 and Donation RM100 . Each tier is its own product, and the price cell is the amount a donor gives when they pick that tier. 4. Start from the Donation template Forms → New form opens the template gallery → Use template on Donation . That gives you a payment form already carrying a product block, name, email and an optional message. 5.

docs.title: Payment fees: merchant setup guide
docs.description: A step-by-step guide to passing the CHIP processing fee to the buyer. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step.
headings: 2. Tick the payment methods you want to charge for
docs.text: A step-by-step guide to passing the CHIP processing fee to the buyer. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: you set your acquirer rate per payment method. JomForm adds the fee on top of the price and grosses the total up, so you still receive the full asking amount. The buyer sees the fee, the method and the final total before paying. 1. Open Settings → Payment fees Settings is in the left sidebar. The Payment fees tab sits between e-Invoice and Webhooks . Only workspace admins and owners see it. 2. Tick the payment methods you want to charge for One row per method: FPX , Card , e-Wallet , DuitNow QR . Ticking a row is what enables the fee for that method; a method with no tick is passed through at cost. 3. Enter your rate - Fixed (sen) : a flat fee in sen. 100 = RM1.00. - Percent (basis points) : 100 = 1%, 200 = 2%, 140 = 1.4%. You may use one or both. The rate you type is the rate the buyer pays; the total is grossed up so the fee comes out of the buyer's side, not yours. 4. Acknowledge the disclosure Enabling a method requires this tick. It records that the fee is passed to the buyer and is subject to acquirer and card-issuer rules. JomForm stores who acknowledged and when. 5. Save Saving is immediate: the green Payment fees saved. banner confirms it, and the rate label on the row ( Card 2.00% ) is the rate your buyers will now be charged. No reload is needed. 6. What your buyer sees On the payment form the buyer picks a method, and the summary shows the fee line and the final total before they proceed. With RM100.00 at 2%: Line Amount --- --- Subtotal RM100.00 Processing fee (Card 2.00%) RM2.04 Total RM102.04 The fee is RM2.04, not RM2.00 .

docs.title: QR table ordering: setup guide
docs.description: A QR code on the table, a menu that opens in the diner's browser, and the order arrives with the table number attached. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks…
headings: 1. Add every dish as a product
5. Turn the form into a menu
docs.text: A QR code on the table, a menu that opens in the diner's browser, and the order arrives with the table number attached. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: each dish is a product . A form in payment mode holds one Product block per dish, and the Restaurant menu switch makes that form's own URL render a menu page instead of the plain form. The QR code is just that URL with ?table=N on the end, so the order always knows which table it came from. 1. Add every dish as a product Products → fill Product name , Price (RM) and press Add product . Leave Stock blank for ∞ (unlimited) and keep Type on One-time . Repeat once per dish, one product per line item on the menu. 2. Check the catalogue The list is now the source of truth for the menu: Nasi Lemak RM12.00, Char Kway Teow RM14.00, Teh Tarik RM3.50 and Roti Bakar RM5.00. The PRICE (RM) column is exactly what the diner pays, so fix a price here rather than in the form. 3. Start from the F&B template Forms → New form → F&B Order + Payment → Use template . The template arrives as a payment form (a Section intro, one Product block, then Name / Email / Phone / Special instructions), which is the shape a menu checkout needs. 4. One Product block per dish In the builder, click Product under PRICING FIELDS once per dish. With a Product block selected, BLOCK SETTINGS → Product is the dropdown that binds the block to the dish, and Text / label is the name the diner sees. Four dishes means four Product blocks. 5. Turn the form into a menu Form Settings → Restaurant menu → Enable restaurant menu.

docs.text: A registration form that takes a one-time fee today and a monthly class fee after that. Every screenshot here was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: a tuition class needs two different amounts: a registration fee paid once, and a monthly fee that repeats. JomForm products carry both shapes, One-time and Subscription . The form holds one Product block per fee, so the parent sees both lines on the same page and one checkout covers them. 1. Make the monthly fee a Subscription product Products → Product name + Price (RM) , then switch Type from One-time to Subscription . The row expands into the recurring controls: Billing period ( Monthly here), Trial days , Billing count ( Infinite (recurring) or Fixed N times ), and Next charge date ( From the day it succeeds (drifts if late) , or keep the original dates and collect or skip missed months). 2. Add the one-time registration fee Add the registration fee with Type left on One-time . The list now shows the two shapes side by side: One-time RM50.00 and Subscription · Monthly RM150.00. That difference is the whole tuition story, one charge to confirm the seat and one charge that repeats every month. 3. Start from the Tuition Class Registration template Forms → New form → Tuition Class Registration → Use template . The template arrives as a payment form with a Section intro ( pay the registration fee to confirm your seat ) and one Product block. It also carries Student name , Parent email , Parent phone and Subject / level . 4. Bind both fees to the form Select the Product block, then BLOCK SETTINGS → Product picks the fee it sells, here Yuran pendaftaran (sekali) .

docs.title: Wedding page and RSVP form: setup guide
docs.description: A step-by-step guide to putting a wedding page and an RSVP form online with JomForm. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step.
headings: 3. Set Form mode to Response form
4. Add the questions and mark the required ones
docs.text: A step-by-step guide to putting a wedding page and an RSVP form online with JomForm. Every screenshot below was captured from the running product; the red box marks the control you touch at that step. What this does: an RSVP collects answers, not money, so the form runs in response mode. The couple gets a page with a title, a short invitation line and the questions they need answered: who is coming, how many guests, and a message. The form has its own public link, so it can go straight into a WhatsApp invitation, and it can sit behind a full landing page (see the Notes). 1. Start a new form Forms → New form . Every form in JomForm starts here. The list on this page holds the drafts and the published forms of the workspace you are in (its name is at the top right: Panduan Demo here). 2. Choose Blank form New form opens the template gallery. There is no wedding template in it, so start from Blank form . The gallery's other cards (Event Registration, Donation, F&B Order + Payment, Tuition Class Registration, …) are for the other showcases. A blank form gives you an empty canvas and the full field palette. 3. Set Form mode to Response form In the builder, the mode sits in the top bar next to the slug : the button reads Payment form , the default. Press it and pick Response form . You do not need to select a block or open the settings panel to reach it. The change asks you to confirm first, and says what it is about to do. Response form collects responses only, with no products and no payment. Leave it on Payment form and the form will expect a product to sell, while an RSVP has nothing to sell. 4. Add the questions and mark the required ones Click a field in the palette on the left to add it to the form.

docs.title: Workspaces & deleting one
docs.description: What a workspace owns, its public address, its currency and exchange rates, how you create one, and what moving one to the Trash (and deleting it for good) requires.
docs.text: Workspaces — JomForm Docs What a workspace owns, its public address, its currency and exchange rates, how you create one, and what moving one to the Trash (and deleting it for good) requires. What a workspace is A workspace holds your forms, products, sales, CHIP credentials, domains and settings. Data never crosses between workspaces. Each workspace has its own public host: your forms are served from {slug}.jomform.com, or a custom domain you add. With no workspace yet, the dashboard asks you to create one on your first sign-in: name it, pick a slug, then create a form. Joined before workspaces existed? JomForm creates one on your next sign-in, named after the first five characters of your email address, and moves your forms in. Your forms then serve from that workspace's address. A form has exactly one public host, so share the new link. Create more from the switcher in the top bar (New workspace). A new workspace starts empty: no credentials, no products, no sales. Renaming a workspace Name and address are two fields with two authorities, both editable in Settings → Workspace. The NAME is only what you and your team see in the dashboard and switcher. Anyone with the manage or admin role can change it. Up to 120 characters, counted in characters rather than bytes, so Chinese, Tamil, Arabic or accented names measure the same. The ADDRESS is your public host on a QR stand, an embed or an affiliate link. Only the OWNER can change it. It must be 3–40 characters of a-z, 0-9 and dashes, cannot end in jomform, and cannot be an address another workspace holds. That includes an address a workspace has renamed away from: it still answers for its own merchant. A reserved name is refused with the reason stated; see reserved names.

docs.title: Activity log
docs.description: The per-workspace audit trail: every recorded action in your workspace, newest first, filterable by event type and date. What it records, what it never records, how long rows are kept, and how the same data is read over the REST API and MCP.
docs.text: Activity log — JomForm Docs The per-workspace audit trail: every recorded action in your workspace, newest first, filterable by event type and date. What it records, what it never records, how long rows are kept, and how the same data is read over the REST API and MCP. What the activity log is Activity records what happened in the workspace you have selected. It is append-only and read from the top, newest first. Forms created, published, restored and purged. Products edited, archived and deleted. Sales captured, confirmed and refunded. API keys and webhook endpoints added and revoked. Domains added and verified, and agent tool calls. Workspace changes such as a deletion. It matters most for the destructive actions. Deleting a workspace and its payment account is permanent, and so is a form purge or a product delete. The log is the only place in the product where you can see afterwards that one happened, which workspace it named, and who did it. Without it, the only way to read that record is a hand-made REST call with an API key, or an MCP client. The trail is per workspace, not per user. Everyone who can reach the workspace sees the same rows. It answers what has happened to this workspace, so switching workspaces in the top bar shows the new one's history. A workspace you are not a member of is never readable here. Reading and filtering it The table has three columns: what happened, the event's own detail, and when it happened. The first column is worded for people — “Workspace deleted” — and the raw event name (workspace.deleted) is the row's tooltip, as REST and MCP use it. The detail is the small JSON payload the action recorded: a form id and slug, a ref code and amount, or a key name.

docs.title: Sales, responses & analytics
docs.description: The Sales page: every sale and every response in one list, per-form counts, partial refunds, and the realtime notifications and order-screen beep.
docs.text: Sales, responses & analytics — JomForm Docs The Sales page: every sale and every response in one list, per-form counts, partial refunds, and the realtime notifications and order-screen beep. Sales Each row carries the reference code, status, buyer, amount, method and date. A status is pending, confirmed, failed or refunded. From here you confirm bank transfers, capture or release skip-capture authorisations, refund in full or in part, and export to CSV. Amounts stay in the currency the sale was recorded in: US$24.90 for a USD sale, RM24.90 for an MYR one. The workspace's current setting never relabels history. GET /v1/rest/sales and list_sales carry it as currency, and a refund is asked for in that same currency. A form's mode names its entries. A payment form offers Sales; a response-only form offers Submission. Both open the same per-form list. GET /v1/rest/forms reports the mode as mode. One list for sales and responses With no form filter the page is the whole record set: every sale and every response, newest first, under one combined count. Filter by a form to see that form's own entries. A response form switches the table to the answer columns. Export CSV writes the same rows with the same filters. A combined export adds a record_type column (sale or submission). Money columns are total, refunded and outstanding, in the sale's own currency. The dashboard's recent list and the MCP tools list_sales and export_sales_csv read the same rows, so the page, the CSV and your agent never disagree. Responses (response-only forms) Set the form mode to response in the builder: no products, no payment. Entries are stored as responses and still appear on the Sales page. Open a response form from Forms → Submission to see when each entry arrived, plus the buyer and the answers.

docs.title: Subscriptions & recurring billing
docs.description: How JomForm recurring billing works: billing periods, a fixed number of charges, the next-charge schedule modes, the retry ladder, failed-card recovery, and the notifications a merchant receives.
docs.text: Subscriptions & recurring billing — JomForm Docs How JomForm recurring billing works: billing periods, a fixed number of charges, the next-charge schedule modes, the retry ladder, failed-card recovery, and the notifications a merchant receives. How a subscription is created A product is a subscription when its type is subscription and it carries a billing period. At checkout JomForm records the sale as a subscription, tokenizes the card with the gateway, and copies the product's period and amount. The first payment is the buyer's checkout, so it counts as charge 1. A background sweep runs every hour. It finds subscriptions whose next charge date has passed and charges the saved card. When the gateway confirms, the charge is marked paid and the next charge date advances by the billing period. A product with a fixed number of charges completes once the last charge is paid. Recurring billing is card-based. The card is saved at checkout, which is what allows later charges without the customer present. A card that can be charged again later. Without one there is nothing to charge on the next period. Your gateway account needs valid credentials. Recurring charges use the same ones as the first payment. Billing period Set the billing period on the product: monthly or yearly. It decides how far the next charge date moves after each successful payment. The period is read from the product at checkout and stored on the sale. A later change to the product never alters an existing subscription's schedule. A fixed number of charges By default a subscription bills indefinitely. Set the number of charges on the product for a fixed term: three months, six sessions, a one-year course.

docs.title: Shipping by zone
docs.description: Charge a delivery fee per delivery zone: workspace-managed zones (state, district or postcode range) with rate rows, weight bands and a free-shipping threshold, resolved from the buyer's address at checkout into sales.shipping_sen.
docs.text: Shipping by zone — JomForm Docs Charge a delivery fee per delivery zone: workspace-managed zones (state, district or postcode range) with rate rows, weight bands and a free-shipping threshold, resolved from the buyer's address at checkout into sales.shipping_sen. Setting it up Create a zone set in Form Settings → Shipping. Name it, tick Default if it should be offered first, and several forms can share it. Add zones. Each zone has a name and at least one rule: a state list, a postcode range or a district list. Any one match is enough. Price each zone with at least one rate row: ringgit, stored as integer sen, an optional name and an optional weight band in grams. Point the form's shipping block at the set and map which blocks carry the state, district and postcode, adding a select if needed. With no mapping the client envelope applies. Decide the no-match outcome: Reject refuses the order and creates no sale; Default charges the fallback zone's rate. There is no third behaviour. Optional: set a free-over amount on a rate row. Once the items subtotal reaches it the fee is zero, and the sale records the threshold crossed. Priority orders the zones, lowest first, so a postcode exception is tested before the state zone around it. The fallback tick is used only when no zone matches. A set is refused for deletion while a form's shipping block points at it, and the refusal names the form. Re-point the block first. Zones and rate sources A shipping block has a rate source. Static list is the default and unchanged: it keeps its own choices and prices, and the chosen price is a line item. Managed zones renders your zone set: each zone with the price of its first rate. The buyer's pick confirms where they are, and the address sets the fee.

docs.title: Processing fees paid by the buyer
docs.description: Set your own acquirer rate per CHIP payment method (fixed sen and/or basis points). The fee is grossed up so you receive the full asking amount, and the buyer sees the method, the fee and the final total before paying.
docs.text: Processing fees paid by the buyer — JomForm Docs Set your own acquirer rate per CHIP payment method (fixed sen and/or basis points). The fee is grossed up so you receive the full asking amount, and the buyer sees the method, the fee and the final total before paying. Setting it up Decide whether you may pass the fee on. Card-network, acquirer and consumer-law rules apply, and the price shown must be the price paid. JomForm does not block it. Type your own rate per method in Settings → Payment fees. FPX, Card, e-Wallet and DuitNow QR each take a fixed sen amount and/or basis points. Tick the acknowledgement. It is recorded with your account, the time and who accepted. Until then no fee reaches a buyer, even with rates saved. Pick which forms carry it. A workspace-wide rate applies to every published payment form; a single form can opt out with its fee override. Watch what the buyer sees: the subtotal, a fee row naming the method and its rate, and the final total, all before Proceed to Payment. The sentence you accept is “I understand this processing fee is passed on to the buyer and is subject to acquirer/card-issuer rules.” It is served by the API. Units are exact: RM1.00 = 100 sen, and 100 basis points is 1%, 140 is 1.4%, 200 is 2%. A fixed amount and a percentage can be combined. The rate is the one your acquirer charges you. JomForm does not guess it, and nothing is filled in for you. Set the override per form in Form Settings or PUT /v1/rest/forms/{id}/fee-override. It applies per form, not per buyer, so the form behaves the same for everyone. If only one method carries a rate it is preselected. With more than one the buyer must choose, and an order naming none is refused rather than guessed.

docs.title: Design → AI agent → MCP
docs.description: Design your form or landing page in a tool like Canva, then use an AI agent (e.g. Claude) connected to the JomForm MCP to apply that design and customize it with CSS and JS.
docs.text: Design → AI agent → MCP customization — JomForm Docs Design your form or landing page in a tool like Canva, then use an AI agent (e.g. Claude) connected to the JomForm MCP to apply that design and customize it with CSS and JS. The flow Design the interface in a tool like Canva, then let an AI agent apply it over the JomForm MCP. Design the form or landing page: logo, hero image, brand colours and a font. Connect an MCP client such as Claude or Cursor to https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp. It registers itself via OAuth 2.1, with no API keys. Upload the assets with upload_media. Apply the theme and the landing page with set_form_theme and set_workspace_landing_page. Set product_image_size and product_image_layout for the product photo. Add custom_css and custom_js for anything the theme controls do not cover. JomForm keeps authority over prices and the payment flow. You design the look, and the agent applies it. Media and custom code Upload images and code assets (css, js, html, svg and woff2) with upload_media. Images are optimised and served straight away. Code assets are scanned before they are served. An SVG must be a well-formed XML document: a browser renders it as XML, so text before the <svg> tag is refused, not stored as a broken image. For full control, set custom_css for styling and layout and custom_js for form behaviour, both through set_form_theme. Custom JS is owner-gated and scanned for malicious code before it goes live. In a custom HTML form it runs on the outer page, and the HTML body stays inert. A blocked script is not saved: the save is refused and names the Custom JS field. The message says which kind of pattern caused it: code execution, obfuscation or beacon code, or an external URL. Remove that part and save again.

docs.title: Custom HTML forms
docs.description: The fully-custom HTML response form: what the sanitizer keeps, how the field-registration contract works, the field types and what the server enforces on submit.
docs.text: JomForm Docs — custom HTML forms The fully-custom HTML response form: what the sanitizer keeps, how the field-registration contract works, the field types and what the server enforces on submit. What a custom HTML form is A custom HTML form is a response-only form whose body is HTML you or an agent supply, instead of builder blocks. The body sits in the custom_html section of the form's config. html is the markup and fields is the field contract. The MCP tool upsert_form takes the two as top-level arguments: custom_html and custom_fields. That is the practical way to write one. A REST create or update can carry the same section inside a raw config map. There is no dashboard editor for this form type, so the write surfaces are the only way in. A form with no html in its section renders through the block renderer as usual. The dashboard does offer Edit on a custom form, which opens the block editor. That editor cannot change or remove the body. Its save carries the custom_html section forward untouched, and the blocks it writes back are not rendered while the section carries html. A custom form is a response form The custom_html section and the form's mode are two statements of one fact. You only have to write one of them. A form that carries an enabled section is response-only. It collects answers and never takes payment. The write surfaces store mode: "response" beside the section for you, on upsert_form and on a raw config map alike. So a raw config whose custom_html has a body and no mode key is stored as a response form, not a payment form. The buyer gets your markup, not the builder or payment layout. Writing mode: "payment" next to an enabled section does not win. The stored mode becomes response.

docs.title: Variation products
docs.description: Sell one product in several options: per-variation price, stock and image, plus a per-variation subscription cycle (monthly/yearly, trial days, charge count) that falls back to the product's.
docs.text: Variation products — JomForm Docs Sell one product in several options: per-variation price, stock and image, plus a per-variation subscription cycle (monthly/yearly, trial days, charge count) that falls back to the product's. What a variation is A simple product has no variations and uses its own price, stock and images. A variable product has one or more variations, and each variation carries its own name, price, stock and image. One T-shirt in sizes S, M and L, or in several colours, is a variable product with one variation per option. A variation is a real row attached to its product, not a field inside it. It keeps the same shape WooCommerce uses. Editing the product replaces the whole list at once, so whatever is in the editor when you save is the authoritative set. Removing a variation removes it. Removing the last one turns the product back into a simple product. Variations are discrete rows, not an attribute grid. There is no size by colour generator: you create each combination you sell as its own line. Price, stock and image For a variable product the variation's price is what the buyer pays. The product-level price is ignored. Set a quantity on the variation to limit stock, or leave it blank for unlimited. A variation that reaches zero shows as sold out on the form and is rejected at checkout, so it can never be oversold. The first image on a variation is its cover in the buyer's option list. The variation's own image is shown next to the option the buyer picks. A subscription cycle on a variation A subscription product can also be variable. Each variation may carry its own billing period (monthly or yearly), trial days and number of charges. That lets you sell Size M, monthly and Size L, yearly from one product, each billed on its own terms.

docs.title: Embed on your site
docs.description: Embed a JomForm form on any website with an iframe. Auto-height via postMessage, the merchant listener snippet, and the 640px fallback.
docs.text: Embed a form on your site — JomForm Docs Embed a JomForm form on any website with an iframe. Auto-height via postMessage, the merchant listener snippet, and the 640px fallback. Embed a form A JomForm form drops into any website with an iframe. It renders the full form: fields, validation and payment. A submit lands in the form's submissions and sales, exactly as it would on the form's own page. The buyer reaches CHIP checkout and the thank-you page in the top frame, so payment works inside the embed. Paste the embed URL, not the form's public URL. The public URL is same-origin only and will not frame. 1. Paste the embed snippet Turn on Allow embedding (iframe) in the form's settings, then paste this on your page. Replace your-workspace and your-form-slug with your workspace slug and the form's slug. With embedding switched off, that address answers 403 instead of rendering the form. Turn the setting on first. 2. Auto-height (recommended) A fixed height causes inner scrollbars on longer forms. The form posts its height over postMessage on load, on resize, and whenever its content changes: conditional fields, product selection, the confirmation message. Listen for jomform:height and set the iframe's height. That is the whole listener. Without the listener nothing breaks: the frame keeps the 640px you set, and longer forms scroll inside it. The form only posts when it is inside a frame. A direct visit to the form URL is unaffected. The message contract Two fields arrive with every message. Filter on type before you touch the DOM. postMessage fields Field Meaning type Always "jomform:height". Filter on it so your other listeners ignore the message. height The form's content height in pixels. Set it as the iframe's CSS height.

docs.title: Email & notifications
docs.description: Receipt emails and per-form notification rules: how a form overrides the workspace, the default notification every new form starts with, dynamic placeholders, and delivery tracking.
docs.text: Email & notifications — JomForm Docs Receipt emails and per-form notification rules: how a form overrides the workspace, the default notification every new form starts with, dynamic placeholders, and delivery tracking. Receipt emails and notification rules Each workspace holds its own email settings, and a new workspace starts with subject and body empty. Any form can override them: subject, body, receipt on/off and merchant notify. Each field offers a use workspace default option, and the resolution order is form → workspace → built-in default. An empty subject or body is not a missing subject. It means JomForm's own receipt, in the language the buyer's form is set to: an English form gets an English receipt, a Malay form a Malay one. Your own words are sent exactly as written, in every language. JomForm does not translate your text. Every new form starts with a default notification to you. Its subject and body start empty, like the receipt fields. A payment form notifies you on sale.paid. A response form notifies you on response.submitted, using the responder's name and email because a response has no sale. An untouched rule shows a grey example, not a wall of text you must delete. The half you leave alone follows the form's language. Switching a form's mode re-points that default notification onto the event the new mode fires. A re-pointed default takes the system's own label for that event. Only the default rule moves, and only while its message is untouched. An edited subject, body or recipient keeps it as written. A form with deleted rules stays silent. The label is a dashboard name, not a decision about the message, so renaming the label alone does not opt the rule out. The MCP tool reference covers the email settings tools.

docs.title: Placeholders reference
docs.description: Every dynamic placeholder you can use in JomForm emails and notifications: {admin_email}, {{ref_code}}, {{amount}}, {{items}}, {{buyer_name}}, {{form_url}}, {{date}}, {{table_number}} and any {{field_id}}.
docs.text: Placeholders reference — JomForm Docs Every dynamic placeholder you can use in JomForm emails and notifications: {admin_email}, {{ref_code}}, {{amount}}, {{items}}, {{buyer_name}}, {{form_url}}, {{date}}, {{table_number}} and any {{field_id}}. Recipient placeholders Used in the Send to field of a notification rule. A recipient is a literal email address, {admin_email}, or a submitted field value. Placeholder Meaning {admin_email} The merchant's account email, used as a notification recipient. The address is resolved at send time. {field_id} The submitted value of a form field, used as a recipient (a buyer's email field, for example). Replace field_id with the field's block id. A recipient can also be a literal address: the Send to field takes one exactly as you type it. Subject and body placeholders Used in the subject and body of receipt emails and notification rules. Each token is replaced with the real value for that sale or submission. {{ref_code}} The sale's reference code, shown to the buyer and used to look up the sale. Empty on a response form: a response has no sale. {{amount}} The formatted sale amount (123.45, in the workspace's currency). Empty on a response form. {{items}} A summary of the purchased items (product names and quantities). Empty on a response form. {{buyer_name}} The buyer's name as submitted on the form. On a response form this is the responder's name. {{full_name}} The name of the person who submitted, buyer or responder. Always defined: empty when the submission carried no name. {{email}} The email of the person who submitted. Always defined: empty when the submission carried no email. {{form_url}} The public URL of the form that was purchased. {{date}} The date the email is sent.

docs.title: Email suppression list
docs.description: How JomForm's email suppression list works: which addresses are never mailed, why each one was added, and how to remove a false positive.
docs.text: Email suppression list — JomForm Docs How JomForm's email suppression list works: which addresses are never mailed, why each one was added, and how to remove a false positive. What the suppression list is The suppression list is the set of addresses JomForm refuses to send email to. Before any message is handed to the provider the recipient is checked against the list. If the address is on it, the message is skipped and the skip recorded. This protects everyone, because all JomForm email leaves through one sending identity: buyer receipts, merchant notifications, verification links and password resets. A high bounce rate on that identity makes the provider slow or pause all of its mail, so a few dead addresses can silence receipts for unrelated merchants. The list is managed by the platform owner (super-admin) on the admin page, and it is also available to a connected AI agent. What gets added automatically The mail provider reports every permanent bounce, complaint and delivery back to JomForm, and those reports feed the list. A hard bounce means the mailbox does not exist. A complaint means the recipient marked the message as spam. Both are added immediately, because sending again can only produce the same result and damage the identity further. A bounce the provider calls temporary is not added on the first event. A mailbox can be full or a server briefly unavailable, and the provider already retried. An address is added only after several temporary bounces within a week, which is what separates a struggling server from a dead mailbox. Addresses are stored lower-cased, so Person@Example.com and person@example.com are the same entry. An address can only appear on the list once.

docs.title: AI spam detection
docs.description: How JomForm's AI spam detection works, what happens to a flagged entry, and how to turn it off for one workspace from the dashboard or over MCP.
docs.text: AI spam detection — JomForm Docs How JomForm's AI spam detection works, what happens to a flagged entry, and how to turn it off for one workspace from the dashboard or over MCP. How AI spam detection works When someone submits a public form, JomForm accepts and records the entry immediately. In the background it sends the answers the sender gave, never the page's own hidden anti-spam fields, to a dedicated AI decision model. It also sends the submitter's email address, the client IP and the form's title. The judge answers with a spam confidence: 0 for certainly genuine, 1 for certainly spam. A score at or above the threshold, 0.5 by default, flags the entry. Nothing about that call delays the submitter. The entry is saved before the judge is asked. A phone or WhatsApp number a sender leaves so you can reply is an ordinary answer, not evidence of spam. An enquiry in Malay, English, Chinese, Tamil or Arabic is judged on what it says, not on its language. A flagged entry carries is_spam with the reason, which names the judge's model, and lands in the Spam queue. There you can un-flag a false positive. The judge is conservative about itself: if the call fails, times out or returns no confidence, the entry stays unflagged. Two things always skip the judge: a submission from a signed-in owner or admin of the workspace, and any workspace that has turned the judge off. What a flagged entry actually means A flag is a suggestion, not a decision. It has two consequences worth knowing before you rely on it. First, the entry is marked. Anything in the dashboard or over the API that reports the spam state shows it as flagged until someone clears it. A flagged entry that is never reviewed stays flagged permanently. Second, a flagged entry is deleted.

docs.title: Trusted devices (2FA)
docs.description: How a trusted device skips the 2FA code for 30 days, how to see every trusted device, and why revoking one is immediate.
docs.text: Trusted devices (2FA) — JomForm Docs How a trusted device skips the 2FA code for 30 days, how to see every trusted device, and why revoking one is immediate. Two-factor authentication (2FA) Add a second factor from Profile → Security. Scan the QR code into an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…) and confirm the 6-digit code it shows. The secret is only activated once you confirm a code, so an abandoned setup never locks you out. From then on, each sign-in asks for the current 6-digit code. Tick don't ask for a code on this device for 30 days at login to trust that device. The password is still required every time. Profile → Security lists every trusted device, with a Revoke button per device and revoke all / log out everywhere. To turn 2FA off, open Profile → Security and click Disable 2FA. You type the current 6-digit code from your authenticator app and nothing else. There is no separate password prompt, so it also works on a session you started from an emailed sign-in link. Disabling 2FA also clears every trusted device, because a device that skipped the removed factor must not keep that exemption. A session started from an emailed sign-in link (a magic link) is treated as unproven. With 2FA on, changing your password, disabling 2FA or adding a passkey asks for a fresh code. A stolen inbox cannot strip the second factor. Each code is single-use. If a prompt is submitted twice, use the next code your app shows. Trusted devices When 2FA is on, tick don't ask for a code on this device for 30 days at login. That device is a trusted device and skips the 2FA code. The password is still required on every sign-in, trusted device or not.

docs.title: In-app assistant
docs.description: What JomForm's built-in chat assistant can and cannot do: it answers questions about how JomForm works and about your own forms, sales and products, it can file a feedback report, and it can prepare a small reversible change for you to confirm — it can never apply a change by itself.
docs.text: In-app assistant — JomForm Docs What JomForm's built-in chat assistant can and cannot do: it answers questions about how JomForm works and about your own forms, sales and products, it can file a feedback report, and it can prepare a small reversible change for you to confirm — it can never apply a change by itself. What the assistant is It speaks the language you write in: English, Bahasa Melayu, 中文, தமிழ் or العربية. The assistant is a chat panel inside the dashboard. Ask it a question in plain language and it answers two kinds of question. The first is how JomForm works. The second is what your account holds: live forms, what a form recorded, sales, submissions and past-due subscriptions. For your account it looks the answer up in your data, with the same tools an AI agent would use over MCP. It is not a general chatbot. It is the assistant for JomForm specifically. Ask how to pass the processing fee to a buyer, how delivery is priced, or whether you can take donations or use your own domain. Those answers come from a short guide to the product that ships with the app, not from whatever the model remembers about other form builders. When neither the guide nor your data can answer, it says so. What it knows about JomForm The product answers come from a short guide that ships inside the app. It covers the questions a merchant asks most. The buyer-borne processing fee and who pays it, plus shipping zones and courier quotes. Products, including pay-what-you-want and donations. Subscriptions and what happens when a charge fails, refunds, and forms that collect responses rather than payments. Custom domains, email notifications, spam review and two-factor sign-in. The MCP server that AI agents connect to, and the REST API.

docs.title: In-app feedback
docs.description: How JomForm's in-app feedback works: file a report or feature request from the dashboard, follow the conversation in the thread, and triage the queue as a platform admin.
docs.text: In-app feedback — JomForm Docs How JomForm's in-app feedback works: file a report or feature request from the dashboard, follow the conversation in the thread, and triage the queue as a platform admin. What in-app feedback is Feedback is a conversation with the JomForm team, opened from inside the dashboard. Every signed-in user has a Feedback link in the sidebar. It is not restricted to account owners, and it does not need a workspace at all. A feedback item is a thread, not a message. You write it once, the team replies in the same place, and you can add detail at any time. The thread keeps its whole history, so you can come back weeks later and read what was said. Use it for a bug, a confusing screen, or a feature your business needs. It is not a way to reach a specific merchant or buyer. Those conversations stay inside the form and receipt features. Where a thread lives A thread belongs to the person who filed it, not to a workspace or a customer account. It is owned by the platform, which is why it never appears in a form list, the Sales page, a CSV export, or any account's spam review queue. The thread follows you, not an account. Change your email address and your existing threads are still yours. Feedback is never subject to the 30-day spam auto-delete that applies to spam-flagged form submissions. A report you filed stays until the conversation is closed. Your threads are private to you. Another signed-in user cannot list, open or reply to a thread that is not theirs. Asking for a thread that is not yours by its id answers the same way as asking for an id that does not exist. What the statuses mean open: filed and not yet picked up. Every new thread starts here. in_progress: a team member has replied and is looking into it.

docs.title: REST API reference
docs.description: The JomForm REST API: create a key, make your first call, then the endpoint reference, webhooks and the error catalogue. Server-to-server only — the API sends no CORS headers.
docs.text: REST API reference — JomForm Docs The JomForm REST API: create a key, make your first call, then the endpoint reference, webhooks and the error catalogue. Server-to-server only — the API sends no CORS headers. Start here The JomForm REST API drives forms, products, sales, subscriptions and webhooks from your own server. Create the key under Settings → API keys: readonly can only read, readwrite can write. The API is server-to-server only: it sends no CORS headers, so a browser cannot call it directly. First call → authentication: create a key, export it, make a request. Look up an operation → endpoints by resource: every operation, generated from the contract. React to events → webhooks: events, signatures, deliveries and retries. Something failed → errors and limits: status codes, throttled routes, versioning.

docs.title: API authentication & scopes
docs.description: Create a JomForm API key, make your first call, and understand key scopes, workspace roles, the missing CORS headers and how to test without a sandbox.
docs.text: API authentication & scopes — JomForm Docs Create a JomForm API key, make your first call, and understand key scopes, workspace roles, the missing CORS headers and how to test without a sandbox. Start in 5 minutes Create a key in Settings → API keys. Choose readwrite to change anything, readonly to read. The raw key is shown once, so copy it when it appears. You can also mint one with POST /v1/rest/keys. Export it in your shell. The API never takes a key in the query string. Make your first call. Every worked example is executed against a live server. A placeholder. This page never prints a real key. One run covers the flow: authenticate, create a form, publish it, read it back, then read the records it made. Authentication A key belongs to a workspace, not a person. Everything it reads and writes is that workspace's data. The dashboard also accepts a browser session cookie on these routes. A script should use a key. The same key drives the MCP server. One credential covers /v1/rest/* and MCP, so see the MCP tool reference. A missing or revoked key gets 401 before any workspace is resolved, so a broken client fails loudly. Scopes A key carries a scope, independent of who created it. It decides what the key may do at all. readonly is read only. Every write is refused with 403. readwrite reads and writes. Inside a ?workspace=<slug> scope there is a second axis: your role in that workspace. A write needs both the key and the role. The payment-credential routes need admin. Scope belongs to the credential; role belongs to the person. The endpoint reference states, per row, which gate applies. No CORS, server-to-server only This API is built for server-to-server calls. It sends no CORS headers at all.

docs.title: API endpoints by resource
docs.description: Every JomForm REST operation, grouped by resource, generated from the OpenAPI 3.1 contract — plus six worked examples the api suite executes.
docs.text: API endpoints by resource — JomForm Docs Every JomForm REST operation, grouped by resource, generated from the OpenAPI 3.1 contract — plus six worked examples the api suite executes. Endpoints: . Expect HTTP , with in the body. Endpoint reference Every route on this page is real: the rows are generated, never typed. Each table carries the route, its access gate and its summary. The published contract carries every request and response schema. Worked examples Each example is executed against a live server, so the status and the body fragment below are the ones the api suite asserts.

docs.title: API webhooks
docs.description: JomForm webhooks: the events, the HMAC and Ed25519 signatures to verify, the delivery log and the retry routes — with the webhook endpoints from the contract.
docs.text: API webhooks — JomForm Docs JomForm webhooks: the events, the HMAC and Ed25519 signatures to verify, the delivery log and the retry routes — with the webhook endpoints from the contract. Endpoints: Webhooks A webhook posts a JSON body to your URL when an event happens. The body is the sale, response or subscription the API returns. sale.paid fires when a payment is confirmed. sale.failed fires when a payment fails. subscription.charged fires on a recurring charge. * subscribes to every event above. Verify the signature Every request carries X-JomForm-Event and an HMAC-SHA256 X-JomForm-Signature header over the raw body. An account with an Ed25519 key also gets X-JomForm-Signature-Ed25519, verified with the public key from get_webhook_signing_key. Deliveries are logged with their status code, attempt number and error. GET /v1/rest/webhooks/{id}/deliveries lists them. Re-send a failed delivery with its retry route; it is queued for the next sweep. A scheduled retry has its own route.

docs.title: API errors & limits
docs.description: JomForm API status codes, the exact routes that are rate limited, the 429 contract, and what /v1 stability means for an integration.
docs.text: API errors & limits — JomForm Docs JomForm API status codes, the exact routes that are rate limited, the 429 contract, and what /v1 stability means for an integration. Errors Failures use the HTTP status for the class and a JSON body that says what went wrong. 400: the request is invalid. The message is written for the caller and may change wording without a version bump. 401: missing, unknown or revoked credential. 403: not allowed. A readonly key on a write, or no role in the ?workspace= you asked for. The body says why. 404: no such object in your workspace. 409: the request conflicts with the object's state. Publishing a payment form with no products returns 409. 429: rate limited (see below). 500: an internal error. The detail is logged server-side and never returned. 503: the feature needs something this deployment lacks. Retrying will not help. A publish 409 carries requires_ack: true, because that form could never take money. Send {"acknowledge":true} to publish it anyway. The body names the reason, and contains the word scope when a scope is the cause. Rate limits Most of this API has no rate limit. Do not design a client around a uniform quota that does not exist. Uploads and the AI routes are limited per client IP. The in-app assistant is limited per user and is session-only. A throttled answer is 429 and carries Retry-After, the seconds that client must wait for that route. Every other route, including the writes, is unmetered. Apply your own backoff and treat a 5xx as retryable. Traffic reaches the API through Cloudflare, where edge protections live. No per-key quota is promised. Nothing meters a client that retries in a loop. Cap the retries and back off; the server will not protect you.

docs.title: MCP tool reference
docs.description: Connect JomForm to Claude, Cursor or another AI agent over the Model Context Protocol, then find the tool, the OAuth scope or the fix you need.
docs.text: MCP tool reference — JomForm Docs Connect JomForm to Claude, Cursor or another AI agent over the Model Context Protocol, then find the tool, the OAuth scope or the fix you need. Start here JomForm speaks the Model Context Protocol. Point any MCP client at https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp and it discovers the tools on its own. The connector authenticates with OAuth 2.1 using an authorization code and PKCE. There are no API keys to copy or rotate. Connect an agent → Claude and Cursor setup. Look up a tool → the full tool list, grouped by what it does. Understand the grant → OAuth and tokens: discovery and scopes. Something fails → troubleshooting: what each refusal means. What an agent can do Each tool names its inputs and outputs. An agent reads that schema and calls the tool directly, so the docs and the server cannot disagree. Tell the agent to read a record before changing it. get_form before upsert_form is the difference between an edit and a lost form.

docs.title: Connect an MCP client
docs.description: Connect Claude, Cursor or another MCP client to JomForm: the remote server URL, the OAuth sign-in, and the JSON entry Cursor uses.
docs.text: Connect an MCP client — JomForm Docs Connect Claude, Cursor or another MCP client to JomForm: the remote server URL, the OAuth sign-in, and the JSON entry Cursor uses. Connect an agent JomForm speaks the Model Context Protocol. Point any MCP client at https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp and it discovers the tools on its own. The connector authenticates with OAuth 2.1 using an authorization code and PKCE. There are no API keys to copy or rotate. Scopes are on OAuth & tokens. Claude Open Settings → Connectors and choose Add custom connector. Paste https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp as the remote MCP server URL. Claude reads the OAuth metadata itself, so the detected client settings are fine. Choose Sign in now and approve the JomForm consent screen. The tools then appear in a conversation. Cursor Open Settings → Tools & MCP → New MCP Server. Add https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp as a remote URL, or edit ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Sign in when Cursor opens the browser; the client stores the token for later calls. Cursor's mcp.json entry. The OAuth sign-in opens on the first call.

docs.title: MCP tool list
docs.description: Every MCP tool JomForm registers, grouped by what it does, with the schema an agent reads. Kept in sync with the api/internal/mcpsrv package by a build guard.
headings: flex items-center gap-2 text-lg font-semibold text-[var(--jf-text)] true text-base 📇 All tools
docs.text: MCP tool list — JomForm Docs Every MCP tool JomForm registers, grouped by what it does, with the schema an agent reads. Kept in sync with the api/internal/mcpsrv package by a build guard. Tool list This page lists every tool the registry registers at this release, grouped by what it does. A guard fails the build if this list and api/internal/mcpsrv drift apart in either direction. The total below is derived from the rows, never typed. A hand-typed count is how the page fell ten tools behind once already. Structured output Tool results come back as structured content. Every tool declares the shape of that result in its outputSchema. All tools declare an object schema. That is what keeps the server usable by a client that validates tools/list strictly. Every listing tool wraps its array in an object: the records sit under items. A paginated listing also carries page, limit and total. So list_products returns {"items": [...]}, not a bare array. Batch tools report their summary beside the per-item outcomes. capture_all_pending_sales returns {"requested", "captured", "failed", "results": [...]}. docs.title: MCP OAuth & tokens
docs.description: How an MCP client discovers JomForm's authorization server, the read and readwrite scopes, and how API-key scopes differ from a connector grant.
docs.text: MCP OAuth & tokens — JomForm Docs How an MCP client discovers JomForm's authorization server, the read and readwrite scopes, and how API-key scopes differ from a connector grant. OAuth discovery A client discovers how to authenticate from the server itself. Every step below is a document or a challenge it can read. An unauthenticated call to https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp is refused with 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…". That header names the protected-resource metadata URL. The client fetches /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource, defined by RFC 9728. The document names the resource, the authorization server, the scopes and the token header. It then fetches /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, RFC 8414, for the authorize, token, revoke and registration endpoints. It registers itself dynamically and opens the authorize URL in the browser, where you sign in and grant access. It exchanges the code for an access token, sending the resource parameter on both requests. JomForm rejects a resource that is not this MCP endpoint, and issues no token. Every later call to /mcp carries the token as a Bearer credential. The resource is https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp. The authorization server is https://mcp.jomform.com, and the scopes are read and readwrite. OAuth connector scopes A connector's grant carries one of two scopes. The MCP client asks for the one it wants on the authorize request. The request carries ?scope=…, space-delimited. JomForm grants exactly what was asked for and records it on the token. Both scopes are advertised in the protected-resource and authorization-server metadata, beside the other fields a client needs. read: read-only. Every listing and getter works.

docs.title: MCP troubleshooting
docs.description: Why an MCP call to JomForm fails: a 401 with no discovery, an invalid scope, a read grant that cannot write, a client that rejects tools/list, or a tool that needs a user token.
docs.text: MCP troubleshooting — JomForm Docs Why an MCP call to JomForm fails: a 401 with no discovery, an invalid scope, a read grant that cannot write, a client that rejects tools/list, or a tool that needs a user token. When a call fails Start with the status code. Each row below is a condition the server refuses, and what to change. MCP failures and their cause You see What it means 401 with WWW-Authenticate No token yet. Let the client follow the discovery flow on OAuth & tokens. 401 after a sign-in The token was issued for another resource. The resource must be https://mcp.jomform.com/mcp. invalid_scope The client asked for a scope JomForm does not advertise. Ask for read or readwrite. A write refused with a scope error The grant is read. A read grant cannot upgrade itself, so connect again and ask for readwrite. A write refused with a role error The key is fine; your role in the ?workspace= scope is read-only. create_api_key refused A read or readonly credential cannot mint a wider one. Use a readwrite credential. The client rejects tools/list Every tool declares an object outputSchema. Update the client; the server will not bend to a strict array check. submit_feedback refused Feedback is user data, so it needs a user token from an OAuth sign-in. An API key is rejected. Read a sale's lifecycle with describe_lifecycle before a state change. An event the table marks enabled=false will be refused.
